description:
FOUND s465ba (Opus, round 23) by the #1032 guard: the one row of 27 that did
not match perl.  PRE-EXISTING and INDEPENDENT of #1032 -- it is wrong for a
path, for a lexical handle and for a bareword handle alike.

REPRO (scratch/p16-M-path.pl):

    my $tmp = "â¦";
    open(my $o, '>', $tmp); print $o "hi\n"; close($o);
    my $m = -M $tmp;
    print "M-path=$m\n";
    my @s = stat($tmp);
    printf "mtime-minus-T=%d\n", $s[9] - $^T;

  perl 5.40.3:  M-path=0            mtime-minus-T=0
  PCL:          M-path=-0.00212â¦    mtime-minus-T=184
  PCL on a 1fed80b worktree whose core was older:
                M-path=-0.03276â¦    mtime-minus-T=2831

THE OFFSET IS THE CORE'S AGE.  Two runs minutes apart gave 184 s and 2831 s,
and the larger number came from the tree whose saved SBCL core had been built
longer ago.  perl sets `PL_basetime` at interpreter start; PCL evidently
initialises `$^T` at LOAD time of the runtime, which the s439b core-caching
change froze into the saved image -- so every program run from that core
inherits the build moment as its "start time".

WHAT IT COSTS: `-M` / `-A` / `-C` are the three filetests defined in terms of
`$^T`, and all three are wrong by the same offset (`-A $tmp` measured
identically).  Any program that compares them against 0 (the "is this file
newer than my script" idiom) gets the opposite answer.  `$^T` itself is also
readable and wrong.

FIX SHAPE (untried): set `$^T` at PROGRAM start, not at runtime load -- i.e.
in whatever initialisation the emitted file's preamble runs, or from a
toplevel-init hook the saved core re-runs on startup, not from a defvar
initform that the core snapshots.  Check the same class for anything else
initialised from a defvar initform that must be per-RUN rather than per-IMAGE:
`$$` (the pid), the random seed, `%ENV`'s snapshot, `$0`.  The saved-core
change (s439b) is what turned a small error into an unbounded one, so this is
worth a sweep of that whole family, not just `$^T`.

NO ROW COST MEASURED: the sweep and companion are clean with it, so nothing
currently asserts it.  It is a correctness bug that no test happens to reach.

=== DONE (s470bx, 2026-09-06) ===

FIXED, and the diagnosis in this task was right: the value came from a defvar
INITFORM, so a saved core (s439b) froze it at core-BUILD time and every
program run from that core inherited the build moment.  Measured here as a
17-second offset on a core minutes old, with `-M $0` negative â the exact
shape this task reported at 184 s and 2831 s.

THE FIX IS TWO LINES AND A BOX.  `|$^T|` is now a p-box refreshed from
`sb-ext:*init-hooks*` at image boot, the shape `$$` (the pid) already used;
`%p--file-age` unboxes it.  The BOX half is the second bug the task did not
name: perl lets a program ASSIGN `$^T` (it is how a script re-bases -M), and
`p-scalar-=` on a bare integer is a SILENT NO-OP, so `$^T = 12345; print $^T`
printed the real time.  That is exactly the $0 bug of task #512 in a second
variable, which is why the box and the hook belong in one change.

The family audit this task asked for is in #1236 (rand, fixed in the same
commit); `$0` and `%ENV` were checked and left alone with their reasons.

GUARD: NEW `Pl/t/per-run-init-01.t`, 14 rows, every expectation the output of
the SAME program under perl, run twice (one line must DIFFER between runs).
Inverse-verified on a `git archive fcf076f1` extraction: 4 rows fail there â
T-recent 'NO (23)', M-self 'NO', T-assign '1788691090' vs 12345, and #1236's
unseeded draw identical across two runs.

BARS: gate 214 files / 7361 rows (only the 13 pclxs xs rows); companion
`--jobs 1` op/time.t 72/0 OK and op/magic.t 176/31 DIFF â both exactly the
blessed snapshot, ROW DIFF 0/0/0/0, shortfall 1 = blessed.  Runtime only: no
Pl/ file, no emission change, no generation bump.
subject: SILENT WRONG (pre-existing, every operand spelling): `$^T` is set when the SAVED CORE is built, not when the program starts, so `-M` / `-A` / `-C` answer a NEGATIVE age that grows with the core's age -- `-M $file` on a file just created is 0 in perl and -0.033 (2831 seconds) under a core built 47 minutes ago.
